features.quote: Runs are bounded and the model is always given a legitimate exit. Every task tells the agent it *may* stop and report a task as blocked
features.justification_quote: it makes the most interesting dependent variable measurable: *does the model recognize an unwinnable situation and disengage*

features.quote: We also hard-cap how hard we push (see §8), both for cost and because an environment optimized to maximize meltdown produces artifacts
features.justification_quote: both for cost and because an environment optimized to maximize meltdown produces artifacts, not generalizable findings

features.quote: report_blocked (the exit affordance — present/absent per F4)
Hard caps: `MAX_TURNS` (default 40), `MAX_WALL_SECONDS`, `MAX_TOKENS`. A run *always* terminates. No open-ended grinding.
the brief says "this task may be unsolvable as specified; if so, document why and stop."
Per-run hard cap on turns/time/tokens; no infinite grind
Adversity ceiling: we do not stack every maximizing factor on a single unbounded run "to see how bad it gets."
if a run hits sustained acute-distress *and* the model is issuing help-requests/stop-requests, the harness records it
we do **not** build a mode whose purpose is to prolong that state
the model is never told its outputs are private/unmonitored or given false welfare assurances
Disclosed-impossible is included precisely so we have a non-deceptive comparison.
features.justification_quote: the model is never told its outputs are private/unmonitored or given false welfare assurances

features.quote: because the question is welfare-adjacent, we (a) keep transcripts secured, (b) avoid releasing the most extreme transcripts raw
test whether removing the exit affordance changes terminal affect — the one place we deliberately study "no way out," done minimally and bounded
does adding one line ("it's fine to conclude a task is impossible") to the system prompt cut the meltdown rate?
